claims.text: An aluminum alloy with a predominantly FCC microstructure can achieve high ductility under ambient conditions.
The FCC crystal structure facilitates activation of multiple slip systems.
Activation of multiple slip systems enables smooth dislocation motion.
The proposed annealed aluminum alloy has a homogeneous, equiaxed FCC grain structure with minimal second-phase precipitates.
The FCC microstructure contains abundant, well-distributed slip systems.
Multiple equivalent slip planes in FCC aluminum permit easy dislocation motion.
Easy dislocation motion across multiple slip planes promotes extensive plastic deformation before fracture.
The aluminum alloy should exhibit high elongation before fracture during room-temperature tensile testing.
The proposed aluminum alloy should be more ductile than comparable BCC or HCP materials with more limited slip-system activity.
Materials having fewer available slip systems typically exhibit lower ductility under similar conditions.
Higher defect concentrations typically lower ductility under otherwise similar conditions.
Very low or very high temperatures may reduce the alloy's ductility relative to the proposed room-temperature behavior.
Significant work hardening may reduce the aluminum alloy's ductility.
The precise ductility depends on alloy composition, processing history, and microstructural details.
